children: Hotel operators and travel platforms report higher bookings, occupancies and room rates as business events, exhibitions, MICE activity and government movement drive demand across key Indian markets

India’s hotel market is seeing a strong September, with corporate travel, MICE activity, government movement, exhibitions and major business events contributing to higher demand across metros and large tier-two cities.

The increase is particularly visible in Delhi, where the BRICS Summit has added significant pressure on room inventory and rates, while Mumbai and other business destinations are also benefiting from a busy events calendar. Recent industry reports have highlighted sharp increases in Delhi hotel prices and tightening availability around the September 12-13 BRICS Summit.

According to Bhanu Chopra, Founder and Managing Director, RateGain Travel Technologies, bookings through RateGain's platform increased 36 per cent by volume and 82 per cent by value during the first eight days of September compared with the same period in August.
The difference between booking volume and value points to a shift towards larger and longer reservations. Chopra attributes part of this movement to conference and exhibition demand.

Travel and hospitality management company CoTrav is also seeing increased activity. Vinod Kumar Sah, Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, says corporate events, MICE and travel activity from existing clients has grown by 20-30 per cent through the year into September, while activity from new clients has risen 50 per cent during the month.
“Overall, our September business is up by over 70 per cent compared to September 2025,” Sah says.

Hotel performance indicators are also reflecting the increase in demand. Animesh Kumar, Commercial Head, Ibis and Ibis Styles, says occupancy across the brands' Indian properties during the first 10 days of September was up 8-10 per cent, while average daily rates increased 16-18 per cent compared with the same period last year.

The movement is particularly pronounced in markets with strong corporate and events calendars. Mumbai has benefited from the Global Fintech Fest 2026, held from September 8 to 11, while Delhi's event calendar includes Semicon India 2026 from September 17 to 19.

Delhi has also experienced a significant rate increase around the BRICS Summit. Cleartrip reports that luxury hotel rates in the capital rose 59 per cent year-on-year, while four-star hotel rates increased by around 113 per cent. Budget bookings were also reported to be up 138 per cent from a year earlier.

Independent coverage around the summit has similarly pointed to limited room availability and substantial increases in Delhi's luxury hotel rates, with some properties quoting rates above ₹2 lakh per night during the peak period.

Bharatt Malik, Senior Vice President, Air and Hotel Business, Yatra Online, says commercial exhibitions and MICE events are supporting demand in Mumbai, with core hotels recording an increase of around 5 per cent in booking volumes.

The impact of MICE is extending beyond the major metros. Gajesh Girdhar, Chairman, Governing Council and Founder Member, Network of Indian MICE Agents, says MICE rates across India have increased 10-15 per cent year-on-year.

“A lot of events have stayed in India as people are less interested in hosting events overseas,” Girdhar says, pointing to destinations including Udaipur, Jaipur, Srinagar, Mumbai, Bhubaneswar and Goa as markets likely to see increased rates as MICE demand rises.

The trend also reflects the growing role of domestic destinations in India's business-events ecosystem. As companies and organisers evaluate destinations for conferences, incentives and exhibitions, hotels in established MICE markets are benefiting from a combination of corporate movement and event-led travel.

In Delhi, hotels are expecting the strong demand to extend beyond the peak BRICS dates. The LaLiT New Delhi is anticipating a sold-out period around the summit, while General Manager Vishal Sharma says the wider September calendar is also supporting hotel performance.

“Compared to several other months, September is expected to perform strongly in terms of occupancies and rates supported by international business travel, government and corporate movement and the overall calendar of events in the capital,” Sharma says.

For India's hotel sector, the September performance highlights the impact that a concentrated business and events calendar can have on room demand and pricing. With corporate travel, exhibitions, conferences, government movement and MICE activity converging across multiple markets, event-led travel is emerging as an important contributor to hotel performance.

The trend is particularly visible in Delhi and Mumbai, but the wider movement across destinations such as Udaipur, Jaipur, Srinagar, Bhubaneswar and Goa points to a broader opportunity for India's hospitality sector as business events increasingly drive travel beyond traditional corporate hubs.
